items.title: This teen took over her family's budget and saved $2,000
paras: Molly's mum handed over the reins of her family's finances. ( ABC News: Fiona Purcell )
When family budgets are stretched, well-intended parents might be tempted to shield their children from financial pressures, but research suggests this could be doing them a disservice.

"Young people raised in households where money is discussed openly are more than twice as likely to feel on top of their finances," said Katrina Samios, the Financial Basics Foundation chief executive.
"Parents often say they don't want to do it because they don't want to stress their kids out, but it actually has the opposite effect.
"The research has shown for many years that the children in those families where money conversations happen at home always show a higher level of financial literacy and capability."
For 15-year-old Molly from Wollongong, NSW, learning about money went well beyond casual conversation at the dinner table.
Taking part in ABC iview show Teenage Boss: Next Level , Molly was challenged to stretch every dollar in her family's budget across one month.
Molly (right) with her mum, Katrina, and sisters Daisy (left) and Bonny. ( ABC News: Fiona Purcell )
Molly took red meat off the menu and replaced it with fish caught by the family — much to the disappointment of her younger sisters, Daisy, 14, and Bonny, 12.
Mum Katrina's weekly "me time" dinners were scrapped, as was spending on extras like clothes and make-up.
And while it wasn't all plain sailing, Molly's frugality meant she was able to save just shy of $2,000.

Handing over the household budget to a teenager might sound alarming to some, but financial literacy experts say there's merit in including children in family financial conversations and giving them opportunities for hands-on experience from an early age.
With cost-of-living pressures and interest rate increases forcing some families to reassess their spending, Ms Samios says "honest and age-appropriate" conversations are important.
When talking about budget changes, she suggests being optimistic with a focus on stability and problem-solving to remove the adult burden of financial stress.
"Kids can handle clarity better than they handle vague stress," Ms Samios said.
"So, you frame it as a plan, not a crisis: 'Things have changed, so we're adjusting our spending to stay secure.'

"If you frame it as the reductions are part of your plan and we're adjusting so that we stay on track, this really helps build that resilience and helps young people understand why things may be changing."

For younger children, Ms Samios suggests explaining your budget in broad categories like food, transport, bills and fun: "Young kids don't need to have spreadsheets, but they do benefit from simple transparency."
However, not all parents are in a position to teach money management skills, points out Ferdi Botha from the Melbourne Institute of Applied Economic and Social Research.
"Age-appropriate school programs teaching basic financial literacy skills are therefore also important," Dr Botha said.
"Ideally, children's financial capabilities should be developed through financial socialisation at home as well as through targeted financial literacy programs at school."
Ms Samios says talking with children about money doesn't mean burdening them with financial worries. ( ABC News: Fiona Purcell )
Contrary to what many parents might expect, Molly wasn't anxious about having visibility of the family's finances.
"I really enjoyed it. I've learned a heap about money and spending and saving," she said.
Managing the family grocery budget, meal planning and cooking each night also gave Molly some insight into the pressures that many parents face.
"Trying to make everyone happy, like peacekeeping and stuff, I felt that was hard," Molly said.
"Daisy and Bonny were upset that there wasn't food that they wanted to eat and I was just making heaps of vegetarian curries and stuff like that."
Molly, pictured with her friend Ayda, also did the meal planning, grocery shopping and cooking. ( ABC iview )
While Molly's belt-tightening was effective, even she admits it isn't sustainable in the long term.
Molly may have been the one budgeting and tracking expenses, but the experience taught the whole family valuable lessons.
Molly took charge of the family’s budgeting and expense tracking for one month. ( ABC News: Fiona Purcell )
Daisy came away with a clear rule about responsible spending: "If you don't have the money, you shouldn't get it," she said.
And for Molly, she found the practical money management experience "very beneficial", and questions whether shielding kids from everyday financial conversations can get in the way of their learning.
"Talking openly about what you're doing — and not making money so much of a hush-hush concept … it's important for everybody to know because it's a big part of life," she said.
We've got a story for you. Stream Teenage Boss: Next Level now on ABC iview .

items.title: Australia’s worst auction market since 2020
paras: The bottom has well and truly fallen out of Australia’s auction market, with Cotality’s final clearance rate for last weekend collapsing to only 43.6% nationally, the worst result since late June:
Auction volumes were also tracking 42% lower than the same weekend last year. Every capital that held auctions last week had a lower clearance rate than a year earlier.
The October average final clearance rate has plunged to only 45%, the lowest result since April 2020 during the height of the COVID lockdowns:
Sydney’s auction market has sickened, with its final clearance rate plunging to only 41.7% last week, the equal worst weekly result since mid-June.
Sydney’s October average clearance rate has fallen to 47%, the weakest result since June 2026 (45%).
Melbourne’s auction market has performed better, tracking just above 50% for four months. However, it has also weakened, falling to 51% in October from 54% in August and September.

Brisbane’s auction market is easily the weakest of the East Coast capitals. Brisbane’s final clearance rate has tracked below 40% since May and averaged only 25% in October, the softest result since April 2020.

This weekend, 1,793 homes are scheduled to go under the hammer across the combined capitals. Auction volumes are expected to be 4.2% lower than the 1,871 auctions held last week and 15.0% lower than the 2,109 held in the same week last year.
Given the widespread expectation that the Reserve Bank will hike interest rates again on Tuesday, I expect another soft result.

Share A A A Australia’s sharemarket has stumbled at the finish line but has closed the week higher as a rebound in recently neglected bank stocks continues.
The S&P/ASX200 rose 1.3 per cent for the week after rising 16.3 points on Friday, or 0.2 per cent, to 8908.1, while the broader All Ordinaries gained 12.8 points, or 0.14 per cent, to 9025.4.

The ASX200 closed in the green on Friday, and higher over the week. Getty The heavyweight financials sector provided much of the momentum, as investors sought safety in Australia’s banks after US tech earnings raised questions about artificial intelligence’s projected returns.
“Wall Street turned decidedly sour as investors penalised tech heavyweights for aggressive spending and elusive pay-offs,” Moomoo chief market strategist Tapas Strickland said.

The mining sector, a large part of the local market, had a mixed day. BHP edged up 0.1 per cent, while Fortescue slid 2.2. Mining giant Rio Tinto slumped 1.6 per cent after an incident at its Oyu Tolgoi copper mine in Mongolia. A rockfall triggered by a seismic event on Thursday caused three workers to be injured, the company said in a statement on Friday.

Most of the major banks advanced as Commonwealth Bank gained 0.2 per cent, National Australia Bank gained 0.4 per cent, and ANZ Bank closed 0.2 per cent higher. Westpac, which is due to deliver its full-year results on Monday, slipped 1.1 per cent.

Shares in supermarket giant Coles plunged 7.7 per cent after the company’s first quarter sales result revealed that growth had slowed in October, and it highlighted customers were shopping around for value. It also said high fuel costs would add to its expenses, and it expected first-half supermarket profits to be flat compared with the prior period.
Energy stocks advanced after oil prices rose on signs the US might resume military strikes against Iran, risking fresh turbulence in the region that might affect energy flows.

West Texas Intermediate rose towards $US103 a barrel, after swinging more than $US3 in the previous session, while Brent settled near $US115. A top commander briefed US President Donald Trump on military options on Thursday, The Wall Street Journal reported. Trump has repeatedly given signals he might restart airstrikes against Tehran after midterm elections next week. Woodside Energy rose 1.8 per cent and Santos added 1.3 per cent while, among the refiners, Ampol was flat and Viva Energy rose 1.1 per cent.
Technology stocks were mixed, as WiseTech rose 0.5 per cent, Xero lost 2.4 per cent, Technology One fell 1.4 per cent and Codan rose 1 per cent. Data centre operator NEXTDC lost 4.9 per cent.

Overnight, the historic drop for Alphabet’s stock dragged the US market lower after the company behind Google and YouTube reported weaker growth for the summer than analysts expected. The report underscored worries about whether all its huge investments in artificial-intelligence technology would pay off.

The S&P 500 fell 0.3 per cent for its first loss in four days, even though the wide majority of stocks rose within the index and across Wall Street. The Nasdaq composite tumbled 1.4 per cent, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 132 points, or 0.3 per cent.

items.title: The price we’ll all pay for the minimum wage hike
paras: How Chancellors love jacking up the minimum wage, as John Healey has just done in his Budget, by 3.9 per cent. Look, here’s a pay rise on me, he is saying, and it doesn’t even require a penny on tax to pay for it.

Left-wing economists have a word for it: ‘predistribution’, which means trying to achieve economic equality without having to tax and spend (not that there aren’t also numerous benefits on offer the poor as well).
Look, here’s a pay rise on me, Healey is saying, and it doesn’t even require a penny on tax to pay for it

It isn’t just Labour Chancellors who have fallen for the lure of increasing the minimum wage, but Tory ones, too. That is why, following Healey’s latest move, we will have a National Living Wage (for the over 21s) of £13.20 per hour and a National Minimum Wage (for 18-20 year olds) of £11.27 per hour. This is nearly twice the level the minimum wage would have been had it simply increased with inflation since it was introduced in 1999. Initially, the over 22s received £3.60 per hour (which would be £7.20 at today’s prices) and 18-21 year olds £3.00 per hour (now £6.00). Over 21s on the Living Wage will now earn more than £27,000 a year.

How lovely the world would be if you could make everyone richer simply by announcing an increase in their wages. Being Chancellor would be the best job in the world, and Healey would be everyone’s favourite uncle.

Sadly, however, the real world doesn’t quite work like that. Someone, of course, will have to pay for an increased minimum wage. The direct victims, needless to say, will be employers, who will suffer a hit to their wage bill. That may mean less profit, less investment in the business – or staff being laid off. That brings us to the next round of victims: the employees who are handed not a pay rise but a redundancy cheque.

But a minimum wage has a more subtle effect than simply costing jobs. Repeated increases in wages at the bottom lead to a phenomenon known as ‘wage compression’, where the differential between the earnings of the lowest-paid staff and those in high brackets is eroded.

Workers at the lowest end may be receiving a 3.9 per cent pay rise thanks to the Chancellor but you can bet that those higher up the pay scale will be receiving a lot less than that. The 3.9 per cent rise in the minimum wage is, after all, higher than inflation (3.5 per cent according to the Consumer Prices Index) and the average increase in earnings in the private sector (3.0 per cent according to the Office of National Statistics).

When the Institute for Fiscal Studies looked into the issue of wage compression in 2024 it found a significant reduction in the ratio between earnings at the 50th percentile and those at the 10th percentile. It also found a fall in the ratio between pay at the 90th percentile and 10th percentile.
Wages, in other words, are being compressed all the way up a company’s pay structure. The only exception was among firms where there were very large numbers of employees on the minimum wage.
This will please socialists who believe in equality of outcome, but it matters because it is removing some of the incentive for low-paid workers to seek promotions with extra responsibilities.

Why take on the extra stress if you are only going to receive a few extra pounds per week? That makes it harder for firms to find the staff they need, and eventually works against the interests of employees. If you fail to take one step up the career ladder you are never going to advance up it at all.

When Tony Blair’s government first proposed the minimum wage, William Hague’s Tories were dead against it, warning that it would lead to mass job losses. It didn’t. Nor, by the way, did it seem to do anything to reduce the benefits bill, which has risen relentlessly since.

But it is always was crucial at what level the wage was set. Initially, it was at a realistic level. Since then, however, it has galloped upwards to reach a level which is highly distorting to the employment market and, in the longer term, against the interests of employees.

items.title: The oil market should brace for a forever stalemate in Iran
paras: The Iran–United States conflict has now endured about 250 days, keeping global crude prices above one hundred dollars a barrel. Oil traders expect a renewed round of hostilities after the upcoming United States midterm elections.

Both Tehran and Washington prefer a controlled stalemate because bombing would further damage infrastructure, trigger social unrest, and raise prices worldwide. Executives at the top of the global energy industry are already preparing for prolonged high costs and reduced production supply.
Watch for post‑midterm negotiations that could alter the trajectory of the Strait of Hormuz trade flow.

items.title: Liberal plan to scrap Treaty risks 'sending us back', Aboriginal leader warns
paras: Wurundjeri man Thane Garvey has called the Opposition Leader's plans to scrap treaty "extremely hypocritical". ( Supplied: Thane Garvey )
Indigenous Victorians are urging the opposition to reconsider its plan to scrap Treaty legislation if it wins the election.
The Coalition is committed to replacing the self-determining model of Treaty with a government department.
Victorians will head to the polls to choose the next state government on November 28.
Victorian Indigenous leaders have accused Opposition Leader Jess Wilson of using Treaty as a "political football", warning decades of progress could be lost if the historic agreement is scrapped.

Last year, the Victorian government became the first state or territory in Australia's history to sign a modern treaty agreement with its First Peoples, which was hailed nationally and internationally as an historic step for all Australians .
Ms Wilson has vowed to scrap the state's Treaty along with its elected First Peoples' body, Gellung Warl , if the Coalition wins the November 28 election.
Last month she reaffirmed that promise, telling ABC Radio Melbourne she had had "constructive conversations with those involved in the Treaty process".
"We don't see a bureaucracy as a way to deliver outcomes for Indigenous Victorians," she said.
"We want to make sure we are investing directly into the programs and we are doing some work right now around what that looks like in health care, education and our justice system."
Victorian Opposition Leader Jess Wilson reiterated her plans to scrap treaty earlier this month. ( 774 ABC Melbourne )
The Coalition has proposed what it calls a "community-led" strategy that would replace the independent Gellung Warl with a government department overseen by a minister.
Ms Wilson said the department, which would be called First Nations Victoria, would be responsible for meeting and reporting on Closing the Gap targets.
Former Treaty Advancement Commissioner Aunty Jill Gallagher was one of the early architects behind Victoria's treaty design.
The Gunditjmara woman said the Coalition's strategy amounted to a return to the advisory committees that had failed First Nations people for decades.

"We haven't closed that gap because we don't have a body, a voice, that can actually talk to governments, that can actually set up processes to hold not only mainstream organisations accountable, but Aboriginal community controlled organisations," she said.
"The Treaty is about not accepting the status quo, because those advisory committees haven't worked."
Aunty Jill Gallagher was appointed Victoria’s first Treaty Advancement Commissioner in 2017. ( ABC News: Scott Jewel )
Aunty Jill said Indigenous Victorians were only just beginning to get a "glimpse" of the positive outcomes Gellung Warl could achieve.
"If it was ripped away and we go back to those advisory committees … we're going to go backwards," she said.

"It's really hard to put in words and articulate, but for me it'd be like sending us back 200 years ago, in my opinion, as to where we are today as Aboriginal people, as the first peoples of this country.
Historic agreements, like the Treaty of Waitangi, are not generally viewed as something that can be repealed.
Victoria's unique modern agreement is underpinned by legislation which can be repealed.

However, some, including the chair of the Treaty Authority, have suggested the actual Treaty agreement, which received cultural assent under Aboriginal law , cannot be "severed unilaterally" by one party.
"It may not be honoured by a particular party … but the Treaty would still exist," Treaty Authority chair Jidah Clark said in an interview with The Age last month.
In Opposition Leader Jess Wilson's seat of Kew, campaigners from First Nations advocacy group Common Threads have been doorknocking hundreds of homes to raise awareness about the Coalition's plans.

Gunditjmara and Yorta Yorta campaigner Tarneen Onus Browne said they had joined the fight for their elders, including their Nan whose only access to culturally safe aged care was away from Country, where she had lived her whole life.
Tarneen Onus Browne says Treaty puts First Nations people in the drivers' seat for policy that impacts them. ( ABC News: Scott Jewel )

"I just find it really sad that she lived on my own Country for a really long time and she wanted to die there but she's not going to get the chance to because the aged care facilities there aren't culturally safe," Onus Browne said.
Onus Browne said a self-determined Treaty was in the interests of all Victorians.
"I think that's really important for non-Aboriginal people to know — that if you want a better way forward, then it does affect you," they said.
"There's nothing materially being taken away from people with Treaty. It's about putting First Nations people in the driver's seat and for First Nations people to make decisions about our own lives."

At a statewide level, Treaty serves as the underpinning for Gellung Warl to have a seat at the table of Parliament — to advise, inform and engage with the government and the parliament on policies that impact the lives of First Peoples.
It is controlled by the First Peoples' Assembly and also has powers to hold the state to account .
Read more The First Peoples' Assembly was one of the first treaty bodies established, and is made up of 34 members.
Of those, 22 are voted for in general elections open to members of Victoria's Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities.
The other 12 are elected by the state's formally recognised traditional owner groups, who hold reserved seats.
For the past few years, the assembly's work has focused on developing the systems and frameworks that are now in place as part of the treaty.

From here, its role under treaty laws is to advocate for the interests of First Peoples, represent them in treaty negotiations and build capacity in the state's First Peoples, including through awarding grants from funds it controls.
Tasked with helping Victorians learn about the past and the impact of colonisation.
Read more Coming from the Wamba Wamba/Wemba Wemba language, Nyerna means "to sit, to listen, to hear, to remember", Yoorrook means "truth" and Tekluna means "to cure, to heal".

The First Peoples' Assembly will appoint three people to Nyerna Yoorrook Telkuna, who will be tasked with promoting healing and reconciliation through a deeper understanding of colonisation and Victoria's history.
How to say it : 'Nyern-ah Yoo-rrook Terl-kuun-ah' — 'ny' is with top of tongue on roof of mouth.
Read more Meaning "you will do" in the Wadi Wadi language, Nginma Ngainga Wara will consist of two or three members, appointed by the First Peoples' Assembly.
Nginma Ngainga Wara is tasked with scrutinising the state government's progress in closing the gap and monitoring implementation of recommendations from the Yoorrook Justice Commission.
It will also advise the First Peoples' Assembly on practical measures to improve outcomes for Indigenous communities.
How to say it : Ng-in-ma Ng-ai(ay)-nga Wa-ra- ' ng' as in 'sing', 'a' as in 'car '.

In August, these new powers were put to the test when Gellung Warl formally called on the government to axe a controversial bill to remove prisoners' guaranteed hour of open air each day, which passed with Coalition support.
Gellung Warl co-chair Djaran Murray-Jackson warned the bill would disproportionately impact Indigenous Victorians, calling it "inconsistent with the spirit and intent of Statewide Treaty".
Gellung Warl co-chairs Djaran Murray-Jackson (left) and Meriki Onus, who were sworn in earlier this year. ( Image: Gellung Warl )
Under the Treaty Act, the Corrections Minister Ros Spence was given 60 days to respond in writing.
The ABC understands the Minister's response acknowledged the concerns, and committed to continuing to monitor the impact of the reforms.
Wurundjeri man and cultural educator Thane Garvey's people are one of eight Traditional Owner groups negotiating their own local treaty with the state.
He said the prospect of losing Treaty would be "absolutely detrimental" for those who had long-fought for it.
"I can't imagine how heartbreaking it's going to be for some of the elders that are in their 70s, 60s, 50s and older to see this disappear," he said.
"I don't understand how we're meant to come together and unify any further when we're going to take away all the hard work that our elders have put forward."
Thane Garvey says the loss of Treaty would be "absolutely detrimental" for those who fought for it. ( Supplied: Thane Garvey )
For years, Mr Garvey has held Welcome to Countries and smoking ceremonies on the steps of parliament — including for the signing of Treaty last year.
He said Ms Wilson had taken part in these ceremonies in the past, calling her current position "extremely hypocritical".
"Jess Wilson was openly voting yes for the referendum. She has definitely walked through the smoke in my smoking ceremonies at Parliament steps," he said.
He said the debate was particularly painful for Indigenous Victorians who had been "politicised as a race so many times for generations".
"This doesn't hold integrity. This doesn't show real passion around caring for people," he said.
"This really shows, I think, that Jess Wilson is willing to move her agenda around, depending on what it is that people are talking about at the time."
Aunty Jill warned Ms Wilson that if she followed through on the pledge, it would be an unprecedented step backwards.
"If you are successful at the upcoming elections and you do tear up the Treaty, you'll be the first government in the world to ever do that," Aunty Jill said.
Onus Browne said their message for the opposition leader was that it was not too reconsider her stance.
"[Repealing] would be really disappointing for First Nations people and lots of people in your constituents and people across Victoria that really believe in this."

items.title: Rogue taxi drivers accused of exploiting passengers at Perth airport, casino
paras: WA's transport minister says operations are underway to catch non-compliant taxi drivers. ( Gary Rivett: ABC News )
WA's transport minister says compliance checks are being ramped up, targeting illegal taxi operators outside Perth Airport and elsewhere.
One legitimate driver says the illegal operators are finding a way around existing compliance checks.
Transport Minister Rita Saffioti says one driver was fined after investigators used digital card data, and other investigations are underway.

Western Australia's transport minister says compliance checks will be ramped up in an attempt to weed out "bad apples" operating taxis in Perth, with a focus on the airport and the Crown Casino complex.
Rita Saffioti said "secret shopper" style checks and compliance blitzes had already taken place four times this year, and at least one driver was handed a fine.
Investigations were carried out in collaboration with WA Police and Australian Federal Police outside Perth Airport and the Burswood entertainment precinct — home to Perth Stadium and Crown Casino.
Perth Airport is one of the areas authorities are targeting in the compliance blitz. ( ABC News: James Carmody )
Perth taxi driver Jonathan Masih told the ABC illegal operators had found workarounds for compliance checks.
"A lot of drivers disappeared then because they got a network, they just ring each other up and then they don't show up," he told 102.5 ABC Perth.
Mr Masih said illegal taxi drivers taking fares from outside major hubs was a form of wage theft.
Protecting the reputation of legitimate taxi drivers is one of the minister's motivations. ( ABC News: Keana Naughton )
"Some of them are posing as a taxi, the other ones they've got private cars and they're just asking the customer to jump in," he said.
"I've been telling the airport authorities, federal police, Department of Transport, minister's office, but nothing changes."
Mr Masih said he was worried about how illegal taxis would impact unknowing passengers.
"It's not really good for the customers, if there's an accident or anything bad happens there's going to be legal issues," he said.
Ms Saffioti said ensuring compliance was as much about protecting the reputation of legitimate drivers as it was stamping out "bad apples" in the industry.
"We want to make sure … all those hard-working taxi drivers continue to get clientele and aren't impacted by those that are abusing the system."
Transport Minister Rita Saffioti says there need to be consequences for people exploiting the system. ( ABC News: Keane Bourke )
"Now we're able to go through and check data and check charges made compared to distance travelled and we've found some people are abusing that system," Ms Saffioti said.
"As a result, there's already been one fine imposed by the court and a number of other investigations are underway."
Ms Saffioti said there were a number of checks being made including car roadworthiness, driver authorisation and company authorisation.
"We need to make sure that those who are exploiting the system or not obeying the rules are dealt with," she said.

items.title: Forrestania inks fresh ore deal to feed hungry WA gold hub

Share A A A Forrestania Resources has moved to bolster its feedstock source for the company’s emerging gold production business in Western Australia, signing a binding ore purchase agreement with ASX-listed High-Tech Metals for up to 400,000 tonnes of gold-bearing ore.

The deal gives the company preferential access to ore from High-Tech’s Mt Fisher gold project for a maximum of 24 months, providing another supply of future mill feed for the company’s burgeoning hub-and-spoke processing strategy.

Forrestania Resources has secured an additional 400,000 tonnes of ore feed for its s Edna May gold plant (pictured), with first processing planned for December 2026. Under the agreement, ore will be purchased on commercial terms determined by its grade, metallurgical recovery and prevailing gold prices, less agreed treatment and processing charges. The delivery schedules and specific processing campaigns will be agreed between the two companies during the term of the agreement.

The deal represents a key step in Forrestania’s strategy to become a significant WA gold producer by leveraging its two processing hubs at Edna May and Lake Johnston. The company has been assembling a significant inventory of ore sources to feed its two hungry plants, building a global mineral resource inventory that now tops a whopping two million ounces.

Forrestania’s initial focus is on the restart of its Edna May gold project, with first ore processing targeted for December, while its second hub at Lake Johnston is slated for commissioning in early 2027. Ore from Mt Fisher will likely feed the 2.9-million-tonne-per-annum Edna May processing plant, which is significantly closer to the deposit than the 3.2Mtpa Lake Johnson facility.

Management says it is already executing on that strategy by hauling ore from its own Taipan deposit and, under a similar recent ore purchase agreement with Star Minerals, from the Tumblegum deposit to Edna May ahead of the restart. Potential feedstock for the plant also includes the recently acquired Tampia project, which holds a 223,300-ounce resource. In a neat piece of operational history, Tampa’s previous owner, Ramelius Resources, previously trucked ore from Tampa to the very same Edna May plant Forrestania now owns.

Other spokes in the growing wheel include a 285,700-ounce resource at its Lady Ada and Lady Magdalene deposits and the 212,400-ounce British Hill deposit, from which ore has already been stockpiled at the Lake Johnston plant ahead of its own restart.

Forrestania Resources executive chairman David Geraghty said: “The Ore Purchase Agreement with High-Tech Metals continues Forrestania’s strategy of establishing a portfolio of third-party ore opportunities around our processing hubs. As we progress towards the restart of the Edna May gold project, Forrestania is already executing on that strategy through the haulage of ore from our Taipan and Tumblegum deposits to Edna May ahead of first ore processing planned for December 2026.”

The agreement lands amid a strong Australian gold backdrop, with spot prices hovering around A$6000 an ounce. The broader Western Australian market is also seeing a renewed focus on processing hubs and third-party ore, with producers pursuing toll-treatment arrangements and nearby deposits to lift plant utilisation and increase production.

On the corporate front, Forrestania has set a firm deadline for its takeover of Zenith Minerals, declaring its now-unconditional offer, first lobbed on June 9, will close at 5pm (AWST) on November 12. The company has ruled out any further extensions unless legally compelled under section 624(2) of the Corporations Act 2001, which provides for an automatic extension in certain circumstances, effectively putting the clock on Zenith shareholders still weighing up their options.

With 62.04 per cent of Zenith already tucked under its belt, Forrestania appears to be firmly in the box seat as it hunts down the magic 90 per cent ownership mark needed to trigger compulsory acquisition. Getting there would hand the company full control of Zenith and its 675,000 ounces of gold resources, adding another important piece to the puzzle in its broader ambition to build a consolidated WA gold powerhouse.

With the clock ticking down to the planned December 2026 restart of the Edna May processing plant, Forrestania appears to be systematically assembling the key ingredients of a genuine gold production business. Securing multiple ore sources, both internal and external, is a well-trodden path for aspiring producers looking to de-risk their operations and maximise the value of their expensive processing infrastructure.

By locking in a substantial third-party ore source to complement its burgeoning two-million-ounce resource base, Forrestania is not only feeding the beast but also giving itself options. In a gold market where every ounce counts, a flexible and scalable supply chain could be the key that unlocks the door to the company becoming WA’s next successful gold producer.

items.title: Cooling property market delivers $5 billion blow to Victorian budget
paras: The Victorian government is forecasting a drop in tax revenue linked to the cooling property market. ( ABC News: Danielle Bonica )
Reduced revenue from stamp duty and land taxes is expected to shave more than $1 billion off Victorian budget forecasts over the next four years.
A fiscal update blames higher interest rates and "other factors" for the decline in property market activity.
However, there has been a slight reduction to the state's eye-watering debt forecasts.
Victoria's cooling property market has delivered a $5 billion blow to the state's budget forecasts less than a month before the state election.
An average of $1.3 billion a year is set to be shaved from the state's tax revenue over the four-year forecast period, according to a fiscal update handed down today.
"This is primarily driven by downgrades to land transfer duty and land tax, reflecting a decline in property market activity amid higher interest rates and other factors," the update said.

The government is still on track to deliver operating surpluses over the outlook period — but the expected average of $300 million a year is a significant reduction from the $1 billion forecast in the May budget.
And net debt will be slightly lower than previously forecast, owing to a lower-than-anticipated debt position in 2025-26.
Debt will climb to $197 billion in 2029-30, about $2 billion less than previously forecast.
The fiscal update shows annual interest payments will be $8.9 billion this year — $24.3 million a day — rising to $11.9 billion in 2029-30, or $32.8 million a day.

The books spell out nearly half a billion in savings since the last budget and also clarify that a clandestine myki surcharge uncovered by the auditor-general earlier this year, which Premier Ben Carroll said would abolished, will formally cease to exist on January 1.
The tax-reliant state is still expected to capture $9.2 billion in land transfer duty and $7.6 billion in property-related taxes in the current financial year.
The drop in property-related taxes was just one of several risks to Victoria's economic outlook that the report said "have increased in recent months and are elevated".
Falling prices in some parts of Melbourne's housing market is estimated to shrink stamp duty and land tax revenue. ( 774 ABC Melbourne: Simon Leo Brown )

"If net overseas migration declines by more than currently expected, this could weigh on the longer-term economic outlook for the state through fewer consumers, lower education exports and a smaller pool of workers," the report said.
It also warned increased fuel and material costs, some linked to the prolonged conflict in the Middle East, could cause further cost headaches for Victoria's infrastructure projects.
Colin Brooks took on the role of Victorian treasurer in August this year. ( ABC News: Danielle Bonica )
Asked if his government took responsibility for the property market downturn, Treasurer Colin Brooks said the entire country had witnessed a similar decline, particularly in the eastern states.
"This is something that's impacting the whole country, driven by inflation, interest rates and also some changes in the federal budget settings as well," he said.
Mr Brooks said the $2.4 billion operating surplus recorded last financial year assured the state could responsibly deliver projects moving forward.
Melbourne has been at the forefront of a cooling property market , with declining auction clearance rates and subdued price growth linked to a slowdown in investment.
Mr Carroll has vowed to reverse increases to land tax unveiled in 2023 as part of a post-COVID budget repair plan if Labor is re-elected next month.
The tax, along with high interest rates and changing tenancy laws, have been credited with an exodus of property investors from Victoria .

items.title: Trump spruiks economy as farmer-funded ads attack cost-of-living record
paras: Donald Trump talking to reporters before his flight to South Carolina. ( Reuters: Jonathan Ernst )
Hello! Welcome back to our US midterms briefing. It's another day on the trail in the US, so let's dive in!
Click here to see how popular US President Donald Trump is today , and click here for a quick breakdown on what the midterms are all about.
I messaged with North America correspondent Lauren Day about some of the key US Senate races we're watching. Here's what she had to say.
We're going to hear about plenty of races in the coming days. Which do you have your eyes on?

There are too many to mention but I've just been in Michigan where progressive firebrand Abdul El-Sayed is in a tight race with Republican Mike Rogers for a US Senate seat. It will be a test of whether a left-wing candidate can win in a purple state. I'm also fascinated to see whether Democrat James Talarico can turn Texas blue — a holy grail for the Dems.

But the race I’ve really been obsessed with is Alaska. The Democratic candidate there, Mary Peltola, has run on a campaign of Fish, Family and Freedom and is a really fascinating character. But the weirdest thing about that race is the fact there are two men named Dan Sullivan on the ballot, including the Republican incumbent. Trump has been crying foul about "Decoy Dan" and has directed the Justice Department to file a lawsuit seeking to prevent the certification of the results if their Dan Sullivan loses. You can't make this stuff up.

If the Republicans lose either chamber, Trump's ability to advance his agenda through Congress could be severely limited and Democrats will have new power to investigate his administration. They could also vote to impeach the president but would need two-thirds of the Senate to remove him from office, which is very unlikely, even if Democrats win the Senate. But of course, executive orders, agency actions and foreign policy don't need congressional approval so those powers would continue, and Trump would still veto any laws Democrats tried to push through Congress.
Want to read more on Lauren's time in Michigan? She wrote a brilliant deep dive on El-Sayed, which you can find here .
US President Donald Trump might not be up for election at the midterms, but his popularity will have a strong influence over the outcome.
The president's party almost always loses House seats in midterm elections and that trend gets steeper when the president is unpopular.
Historic polling data collated by analytics firm Gallup shows presidents with approval ratings below 50 per cent have seen their party lose an average of 37 House seats.
Presidents with approval ratings above 50 per cent have netted smaller loses, with an average of 14 seats.
Thanks for joining me! I'll be back at the same time on Monday with more.

items.title: North Korean workers sold into Russia then stripped of wages, report finds
paras: The network is allegedly run by Moscow-based businessman Vladimir Sokolov (left). ( Supplied: GRC )
Russian brokers are advertising North Korean workers to companies as part of a forced labour program, a new report has alleged.
It found those involved are working up to 12 hours a day, six to seven times a week, and forfeiting most of their income to the North Korea's authoritarian regime.
The report found some North Korean workers were being sent to "facilities essential to Russia's war economy".
North Korean workers are being advertised online as for sale to Russian businesses as part of a forced labour program, a new report has found.
The workers' wages are being used to fund North Korea's ballistic missile program, and their labour is boosting the Kremlin's war economy, it alleges.

International human rights group Global Rights Compliance (GRC) said it had members pose undercover as representatives of a prospective company as part of a nine-month investigation into a labour-brokering network run by a Russian businessman.
It found the broker network charges a commission of between 100,000 and 150,000 roubles ($1,765 to $2,650) per North Korean worker it places with a company.
North Korean workers in a garment factory that GRC believes to be in Chekhov. ( Supplied: GRC )
The group alleges the North Koreans then work up to 12 hours a day, six to seven times a week, and forfeit most of their income to the authoritarian regime.
It said the Russian brokers have "turned the supply of North Korean labour into an organised industry".
"It's shocking to me, the normalisation of slave labour conditions in Russia," the report's lead investigator, Dylan Carter, told the ABC.

It is the latest in a series of reports to investigate the use of labour from North Korea, in breach of a resolution from the United Nations Security Council, which requires member states to repatriate North Koreans earning money in their territory.

The Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team, an international coalition set up to report on violations of UN sanctions against North Korea, recently found North Korean overseas workers raised between $US450 million ($633 million) and $US800 million last year for the authoritarian state's nuclear weapons program.
It found there could be anywhere between 35,000 and 101,000 North Korean workers overseas, primarily in China and Russia.

North Korea has denied providing forced labour, although organisations, including the United Nations, have documented it. Russia has also denied violating UN resolutions on using North Korean workers, despite several reports documenting it.
The GRC report focuses on a brokering network allegedly run by Moscow-based businessman Vladimir Sokolov.
A website it links to him advertises "Industrial internships for students from the DPRK [North Korea] in Russia".
It found his brokering network places groups of at least 50 workers at companies and receives payments for each worker.
Vladimir Sokolov (centre left) with North Korean officials at an agricultural factory. ( Supplied: GRC )

Undercover GRC investigators were reportedly told by an operations manager working for Mr Sokolov that "North Korean workers enter Russia on student visas, are enrolled at colleges they never attend, and are placed within Russian companies".
A change in Russian migration law in 2020 allows foreign students to work while studying in the country.
"This arrangement avoids work authorisations prohibited under UN sanctions and places workers outside of the protections of Russian labour law," the report says.
The investigation also found the Russian companies must have an official audit visit from North Korean officials before workers are sent there.
"Taken together, the findings show that North Korean labour in Russia is the product of an organised system rather than informal, ad hoc, or isolated labour arrangements," the report found.

The report said there were other brokers bringing in North Koreans, but that Mr Sokolov "distinguishes his scheme" by arguing it is "lawful because the 'students' are undertaking 'work training' as part of their education".
The report authors said they approached Mr Sokolov for comment but did not receive a response.

Another businessman associated with the network denied the North Koreans were workers, saying they were students doing "practical training at production sites" and the payments were "academic scholarships".
He said there was no "forced labour network" and that the allegations were "unsubstantiated" and based on "speculation".
While the majority of North Korean overseas workers are believed to be in China, there has been a growing number going to Russia, as the two countries tighten ties .

The GRC said "economic pressures and demands of [the] Ukraine war" are adding to Russia's need to boost its workforce, and its report found North Korean workers were "being used in facilities essential to Russia's war economy".
Mr Carter said North Korean workers were detected at an aluminium manufacturing plant that had contracts with major defence suppliers.
The GRC also sourced photos of workers at a food manufacturer that produces dry rations for Russian soldiers.
North Korean workers at a Russian factory outside of Moscow that produces preserved foods and military rations. ( Supplied: GRC )
Mr Carter said the photos were from a dog food line, but it was believed the North Koreans were also working packaging the military rations, which came out of the same building.
The workers are paid a proper wage, but it is alleged up to 90 per cent of overseas workers' wages are forfeited to the North Korean regime, helping to fund its ballistic missiles program.
Mr Carter said when the workers arrived in Russia, they faced a "stark and depressing world" where they were monitored and controlled.
"These are arrangements that benefit the North Korean and Russian states very heavily at the cost of North Korean civilians who ultimately pay the price for their labour," he said.
The Russian businessman investigated in the report, Mr Sokolov, has recently been sanctioned by the European Union.

Just over two weeks ago, the Council of the EU added Mr Sokolov to a list of people and entities that are "responsible for supporting, promoting or facilitating activities" that contribute to North Korea's weapons programs and "violating and evading United Nations sanctions".
The sanctions include an asset freeze and a ban on travelling to the European Union.
Vladimir Sokolov's office door has a sign showing the Russian and DPRK flags with a handshake graphic. ( Supplied: GRC )

He was one of three individuals and two entities added to the list, which now runs to more than 100, as part of a focus on activities "linked to the growing military and economic cooperation between the DPRK [North Korea] and Russia".
The council has accused Mr Sokolov of "promoting and facilitating commercial and industrial cooperation projects" with North Korea.
The report's revelations come at a time of heightened tension between North and South Korea, and amid a fraying relationship between Seoul and Ukraine.
North Korea positioned artillery along the demilitarised zone this week, with barrels pointed towards South Korea.
A howitzer with text that translates to "Destroy the US imperialist aggressors, the sworn enemies of the Korean people!" seen along the border this week. ( Reuters: Kim Hong-Ji )
It comes after a mine blast in the area injured three South Korean soldiers. Seoul has called for an apology from Pyongyang, while the latter claimed the incident was fabricated.

As Russia and North Korea continue to tighten ties, Ukraine has been warning that more troops from the hermit kingdom could be sent to join the war and has called for more support from other nations in the region, including South Korea and Japan.
But its relationship with Seoul has come under strain, following a dispute over the release of information about two Nmeorth Korean prisoners of war.

South Korea has withdrawn eight diplomatic personnel from Ukraine since President Volodymyr Zelenskyy revealed the North Korean soldiers were transferred to South Korea after being captured while fighting for Russia, an arrangement Seoul said was meant to be confidential.

items.title: Sectoral Deployment of Bank Credit – September 2026
paras: Data on sectoral deployment of bank credit for the month of September 2026, collected from 41 select scheduled commercial banks (SCBs), which together account for about 95 per cent of the total non-food credit by all SCBs 1 , are set out in Statements I and II . On a year-on-year (y-o-y) basis, non-food bank credit 2 grew by 19.1 per cent as on the fortnight ended September 30, 2026, compared to 11.2 per cent during the corresponding fortnight of the previous year (i.e., October 03, 2025). Highlights of the sectoral deployment of bank credit as on the fortnight ended September 30, 2026, are given below: Credit to agriculture and allied activities registered a y-o-y growth of 19.5 per cent vis-a-vis 8.9 per cent in the corresponding fortnight of the previous year. Credit to industry recorded a y-o-y growth of 19.5 per cent (7.7 per cent in the corresponding fortnight of last year). While credit to ‘large’ and ‘medium’ industries grew at an accelerated pace, ‘micro and small’ industries exhibited steady growth. Among major industries, credit to ‘infrastructure’, ‘basic metal and metal products’, ‘all engineering’, ‘chemical and chemical products’, ‘food processing’ and ‘textiles’ marked buoyant y-o-y growth. Credit to services sector registered a y-o-y growth of 28.3 per cent (9.9 per cent in the corresponding fortnight of the previous year), supported by buoyant growth in segments such as ‘non-banking financial companies’ (NBFCs), ‘trade’ ‘commercial real estate’, ‘transport operators’ and ‘professional services’. Credit to personal loans segment recorded a y-o-y growth of 17.3 per cent, as compared with 11.5 per cent a year ago. While credit growth in segments such as ‘housing’ and ‘vehicle loans’ remained resilient, ‘advances against fixed deposits’ accelerated. Growth in ‘loans against gold jewellery’ and ‘education’ decelerated compared to last year, albeit it remained strong. items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

items.title: Reserve Bank holds 36 th Conference of State Finance Secretaries
paras: The 36 th Conference of State Finance Secretaries was held on October 27, 2026 at RBI, Mumbai. The theme of the Conference was ‘Role of Quality of Expenditure, Effective Cash and Prudent Debt Management in Enhancing States’ Fiscal Sustainability’. The Conference was attended by the Finance Secretaries of 27 States and three Union Territories as well as senior officials from the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, Controller General of Accounts and the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. Governor, Reserve Bank of India inaugurated the Conference. Addressing the participants, the Governor emphasised the importance of maintaining the quality of expenditure to ensure the long-term fiscal health of the States. He also emphasised on the need for the States to adopt prudent borrowing strategies and efficient cash management practices. The Governor urged the States to onboard onto the Unified Lending Interface (ULI) and utilise Programmable Central Bank Digital Currency (P-CBDC) for Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT). He also advised States to make effective use of the State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC) forum. During the Conference, the Governor released a Booklet titled ‘Compendium on Cash and Debt Management for State Governments’. The Booklet summarises relevant concepts, operational processes and good cash and debt management practices in a concise and accessible format. The meeting reviewed, inter alia, market borrowings by the States, short-term financial accommodation to the States from Reserve Bank, adoption of Benchmark Issuance Strategy by the States, etc. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1395

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: "India matters most for future of planet" says British High Commissioner Lindy Cameron
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): In recent times when climate change has become a pressing issue with countries across the world being ravaged due to climate catastrophes, it becomes imperative to discuss and deliberate upon global actions that can help the world rise up and meet these challenges. At the NDTV World Summit's a discussion was held on the theme, "India Matters The Most For Future Of Planet". Participants in the discussion included Erik Solheim, Former Minister of Climate and the Environment of Norway; Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India; Shishir Priyadarshi, President Chintan Research Foundation; Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative. "India is the country that matters the most for the future of the planet and climate change. India's ambition for development should not in any way be constrained by the responsibilities of the planet," Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India, emphasised. She noted that the UK is committed towards the Multilateral Development Banks (MDB) reforms, technology and research support in India to aid the efforts. "Every dollar invested in resilient infrastructure pays 4 times over," said Cameron. "Lived experience of climate emergencies helps people to understand why their government needs to take policy action now," she added. Further talking about the need for urgent government action, Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative said, "Series of disasters affecting both developed and developing countries are serving as a wake-up call. As rich countries will get more and more affected by climate change which they did not imagine till a couple of years ago, most vulnerable countries are going to be struggling with impacts who also have very less capacity to deal with it. India is taking a leadership role in the global fight against climate change. Initiatives such as Global Biofuels Alliance, International Solar Alliance, and Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure are some efforts taken by India in recent years to manage the climate crisis. (ANI)

items.title: "Will work with India to implement solution" says China on LAC patrolling agreement
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Beijing [ China ], October 22 (ANI): China on Tuesday said that it has reached a resolution with India on resolving their border conflict and will work to implement solutions, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson was quoted as saying by Reuters news agency. China Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian told a regular press briefing,"We have reached a resolution on the relevant matter, will work with the India n side to implement the solution. We are in close communication through diplomatic and military channels." On October 21, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) announced that an agreement has been reached regarding patrolling arrangements along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in the India - China border area. The announcement came ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's visit to Kazan, Russia, for the 16th BRICS summit that begins today and is scheduled to run till October 24. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri addressed the media, stating, "This agreement is the outcome of extensive discussions over the past several weeks with Chinese interlocutors at both diplomatic and military levels." He noted that military commanders have been involved in negotiations aimed at addressing the tensions that have persisted since 2020. Misri explained that the agreement signifies a path toward disengagement and a potential resolution of the issues that arose during the significant confrontations in 2020. Misri recalled the clashes between the People's Liberation Army of China and the India n Army , particularly highlighting the violent encounters in June 2020, which resulted in casualties on both sides. He added that this agreement marks a critical step in stabilising relations between India and China as both nations seek to manage their border disputes and prevent further military confrontations. Misri said,"On several areas along the Line of Actual Control, we held discussions with Chinese interlocutors both at the diplomatic as well as military levels through meetings with military commanders at various levels. These discussions had in the past resulted in the resolution of standoffs at various locations. There are some locations and areas where stand-offs had not been resolved." "Now, as a result of the discussions over the last several weeks, an agreement has been reached on patrolling arrangements along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in the India - China border areas. This is leading to disengagement and eventually a resolution of the issues that arose in these areas in 2020," he said. Earlier today, Chief of Army Staff General Upendra Dwivedi addressing an event in Delhi said that restoring trust along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) would be a gradual process, to return to the April 2020 status quo. "We are working to rebuild trust, and restoring that trust will take time," he said, highlighting the steps of disengagement, de-escalation, and buffer zone management as crucial for easing tensions between the two nations. He further explained that the process will take place in phases, with each step aimed at reducing tensions. "This normal management of the LAC will not just stop there. There are phases in that as well," the COAS said. The agreement marks a crucial step in stabilising relations between India and China as both nations work to manage their border disputes and avoid further military confrontations.In early May 2020, troops from China 's People's Liberation Army and the India n Army clashed at locations along the LAC, the disputed boundary between China and India . The situation escalated on June 15-16, 2020, resulting in casualties on both sides. (ANI)

items.title: "High probability of meeting between PM Modi, President Xi": Former Indian envoy on patrolling agreement between India-C
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Gautam Bambawale , former India n Ambassador to China , Bhutan, and Pakistan said that the recent agreement on border patrolling between India and China along the Line of Actual Control ( LAC ) has opened up possibilities for a bilateral meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Xi Jinping in Kazan along the sidelines of the BRICS Summit and asserted that the probability of a meeting between the two leaders is "very high." He also noted that although India and China reached an agreement on patrolling arrangements ahead of the BRICS Summit in Kazan , Russia , this breakthrough is the result of discussions and negotiations between India and China , with no involvement from Russia . While speaking with ANI, Bambawale said, "On this question of the recent agreement on patrolling along the LAC , especially in eastern Ladakh, I do not think the Russia ns must have had a hand in it. It would have been discussions between India and China and negotiations between India and China that led to this agreement." He added, "Now that the problems on the border along the LAC have been sorted out, I think there is a very high probability that our Prime Minister Modi and the President of China , Xi Jinping , could have a bilateral meeting in Kazan . I think it would be a meeting to break the ice. I don't expect some great warmth suddenly. It will take time to rebuild the relationship from the setback that it had in the Summer of 2020. This situation has gone on for 4.5 years. So it will take some time to repair the relationship but I think this agreement will be a start and if there's a meeting between the two leaders at the summit level in Kazan on the sidelines of BRICS, then that will be another step towards restoring the relationship to what it was earlier." Bambawale further said that the agreement on patrolling arrangements implies that China is willing to restore the relationship between the two nations to its pre-2020 state, paving the way for progress in other sectors such as trade, commerce, and investment.

He said, "The agreement has come just before the BRICS summit takes place in the next few days in Kazan in Russia . I think what this implies is that the Chinese side is wanting to restore the relationship between India and China to what it was earlier. It wants the other aspects of the relationship like trade, commerce and investment to move ahead. It will of course take some time to restore the trust between the two countries. But at least I think a beginning can be made and perhaps there might be a meeting at the topmost level between PM Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping at Kazan ." The former India n Ambassador further noted that the agreement between India and China is expected to significantly boost the BRICS grouping, despite not necessarily indicating a closer relationship between India and Russia or China . "I won't say India is moving closer to Russia and China but I think the BRICS grouping will be immeasurably strengthened because of this understanding between India and China because of the cooling of tensions on the border between India and China and as India has always said that a peaceful border means that the rest of the relatrionship can also move ahead. So I believe that a better relationship between India and China will be better for the BRICS grouping," Bambawale told ANI. Bambawale further said, "If this implies that the status quo ante has been restored as it existed before the Chinese undertook the military action in eastern Ladakh in summer of 2020... then I think this is a very welcome development. The government of India should be congratulated on taking a firm position on this matter and that India 's stand has been vindicated after 4.5 years of face-to-face situation between India n and Chinese troops. If it means that the status quo ante has been restored, then we definitely welcome this agreement. It is a good agreement and we can move forward on the basis of this agreement." Notably, a day before, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri, who addressed a special media briefing ahead of PM Modi 's visit to Russia for the BRICS Summit , said India and China have reached an agreement on the patrolling arrangements along LAC . The agreement was reached ahead of the BRICS Summit which will be attended by PM Modi and Chinese President Xi. "On several areas along the Line of Actual Control , we held discussions with Chinese interlocutors, both on diplomatic as well as the military levels through meeting with military commanders at various levels. These discussions had in the past resulted in the resolution of standoffs at various locations. There are some locations and areas where stand-offs had not been resolved," said Misri. "Now, as a result of the discussions taking place over the last several weeks an agreement has been arrived at on patrolling arrangements along the LAC in the India - China border areas. This is leading to disengagement and eventually a resolution of the issues that had arisen in these areas in 2020," he added. (ANI)

items.title: India sends humanitarian aid to Palestine; consignment comprises 30 tons of essential items
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, India took a significant step in providing humanitarian aid for the people of Palestine. This initial consignment comprises 30 tons of essential items, including medicines, surgical supplies, dental products, general medical items, and high-energy biscuits, which will be distributed through the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA). Sharing a post on X, Randhir Jaiswal, the official spokesperson of the Ministry of External Affairs wrote, "India sends humanitarian assistance for the people of Palestine through UNRWA." "The first tranche of assistance comprising 30 tons of medicine and food items has departed today. The consignment includes a wide range of essential medicines and surgical supplies, dental products, general medical items and high-energy biscuits," the post added.

Notably, a few days ago, the World Food Programme issued a warning for northern Gaza, saying that WFP's supplies are depleting. Earlier on October 20, the United Nations renewed its call for an end to the war in Gaza, emphasising the urgent need for the release of hostages, the cessation of the displacement of Palestinians, and the unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid. In a statement released by the UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, Tor Wennesland, the UN expressed deep concern, stating, "The nightmare in Gaza is intensifying. Horrifying scenes are unfolding in the northern Strip amidst conflict, relentless Israeli strikes and an ever-worsening humanitarian crisis."
